description:
This project is a short personal work created during my free time over the course of one week. After several months without opening Blender due to intensive CPGE studies, I took advantage of the holidays to return to the software and avoid losing touch with it.
The main objective of this project was to explore photorealism through an interior brutalist architecture scene. The concrete materials were created entirely procedurally.

The scene setup was kept intentionally simple. Lighting relies on a single sky texture to provide natural and even illumination. A relatively wide focal length of 30 mm was chosen to highlight the architecture, combined with an aperture of f/2.8 to introduce a subtle and realistic depth of field. Due to the wide focal length and a distant focus point, the blur remains barely perceptible.

The scene was modeled and rendered using Blender with the Cycles rendering engine. The images were rendered at a resolution of 2000×3000 px with 1024 samples, for an average render time of approximately one hour per image. The final images were exported in .exr format, in linear color space (Rec.709), before post-production.

Compositing and post-production were carried out using Blender and DaVinci Resolve. This project was also my first one completed on Linux, after switching to Ubuntu a few months ago, where I observed noticeable performance gains compared to Windows 11.

The project was created on a system equipped with 16 GB of DDR5 memory, an Intel Core i7-12700H processor and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050.
